# Qt module licence matrix — the ALLOWLIST a product build is checked against.
# Round 15 #2 killed the previous design and was right to. A denylist of GPL-only module names
# cannot be correct: it only refuses what someone remembered to write down, it ages out with every
# Qt minor, and the version installed here does not even contain six of the names it carried
# (Qt6Canvas3D, Qt6Mqtt, Qt6VirtualKeyboard, Qt6HttpServer, Qt6Grpc, Qt6Coap — measured with
# pkg-config on 2026-08-13). A module invented tomorrow passes a denylist by existing.
# So the polarity is inverted. This file lists the modules whose open-source licence is ESTABLISHED,
# with the source of that statement. A product spec may request a module only if it is listed here
# as lgpl. Anything else — GPL-only, unknown, newly introduced, misspelled — is refused, and the
# refusal names the module rather than a symbol namespace.
# `verified-for` is load-bearing: the gate REFUSES to judge a Qt version that is not listed, instead
# of applying another version's matrix. Adding a version means re-reading Qt's licensing page and
# the SBOM for that exact release, then recording it here. That is the work; this file is only where
# the answer is written down.
# Columns: release<TAB>module<TAB>licence<TAB>source
#   licence: lgpl      — LGPLv3 for open-source users; may be linked into a BSL-1.0 product
#            gpl-only  — GPLv3 only for open-source users; may be used by tests, never by a product
#   Anything absent is neither: it is UNKNOWN, and unknown is refused.
# KEYED BY (RELEASE, MODULE), not by module alone (round 18 #2). With module-only rows, adding a
# `verified-for 6.4.2` line made 6.4.2 silently inherit every decision written while reading 6.11.1 —
# there was no mechanical link between a revision and the answers taken from it. Now a row answers
# for exactly the release it was read against, and an artifact built with another one is refused
# even when a module of the same name is listed.
# NOTE ON Qt 5: the rows below say 5.15.17 because that is the release whose licensing was read.
# This machine builds its Qt5 parity archives with 5.15.19, which is NOT recorded — so the gate
# refuses those artifacts, and that refusal is the honest state rather than a gap to paper over by
# renaming the rows. Establishing 5.15.19 means reading Qt's licensing for 5.15.19.
# Keyed by the EXACT release, not the minor: round 16 #6 measured the gate claiming "Qt 6.11.1 is
# verified" from a row that said 6.11. Adding a patch release means re-reading Qt's licensing page
# and SBOM for it — which is the work; this line is only where the answer is written down.
verified-for
